text:
Jonah: FYI saw a big cross-AZ tail in eu-west-2 this morning around 09:17. 95p token latency jumped ~60% and NIC egress hit 92% on a handful of racks. Tenant 'atlas' triggered a massive prefill and KV cache regen when they pushed a large batch.
Mira: ugh. source of spike = prefill + kvcache regen + bursty egress? any slab evictions?
Jonah: yes to all. HBM slab churned, we saw HBM_evictions spike and NVLINK QoS jittered. core dump of metrics attached to the incident Slack thread.
Anand: Do we have short-term mitigation? can we route atlas to dedicated burst lanes or pin them to a quieter AZ?
Kai: Routing them out of region is possible but has regulatory/data locality issues. We can do per-tenant soft-carve ephemeral slices for heavy batches (fractional dedicated), but that costs more.
Sasha: Proposal: "pinwheel" containment. On surge detection, rotate a tenant's burst allocation across a sequence of racks/azs for N minutes each to spread thermal/egress load and avoid single-rack saturation. Keeps tenant on shared infra but evens the noise.
Mira: interesting. so tenants still multi-tenant but their "hot" working set hops around? does that disrupt KV cache warmness?
Sasha: It does, but we think prefix/KV caching + short warmup prefill can be tuned. idea is short hops (3-5m) so we avoid long-term cache miss penalties. Also we only rotate when egress or slab thresholds exceeded.
Anand: Metrics we would watch: egress_bytes_per_nic, hbm_slab_evictions, kvcache_miss_rate, p95_token_latency, and prefill_ops/sec. Alert when any > 80th pctile of historical for > 60s.
Riley: Any changes needed in scheduler? sounds like we need a rotation controller that can mark a tenant as "pinwheel-burst" and annotates allocations. Also need a graceful drain hop.
Kai: scheduler changes are modest: add tenant tag + eviction/reshuffle window. But we need to ensure dedicated pools and reserved capacity aren't impacted. Priority: pinwheel should only use ephemeral fractional slices, not reserved dedicated pools.
Jonah: Runbook stub: detect surge -> mark tenant pinwheel -> allocate ephemeral burst slice on target rack -> warm prefill (limit 2 queued prefill jobs) -> shift after 4m -> monitor lat/egress -> if repeated, fallback to dedicated carveout + billing.
Mira: cost question: how much extra egress/cold KVC cache overhead? we need an estimate for SRE leadership.
Sasha: back-of-envelope: distributing the workload reduces peak egress per-rack by ~40% on our test harness, but increases total prefill-related tokens by ~10% due to cache churn. If held to short rotations, net token cost up ~5-8% vs current worst-case outage.
Anand: sounds acceptable compared to provisioning a dedicated pool for every noisy tenant. 
Riley: we should add a canary: enable pinwheel for test-tenant 'pinwheel-canary' for 24h in eu-west-2 during low-traffic window. Monitor p95, slab_evictions, and billing tokens.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary job queued: infra/pinwheel-controller -> canary/pinwheel-canary -> scheduled 23:00 UTC.
Kai: ops-bot, make sure we have a rollback toggle exposed in console and a per-tenant throttle cap.
ops-bot: noted. rollback toggle and tenant throttle cap exposed as runtime flags: pinwheel.enabled, pinwheel.max_prefill_qps, pinwheel.rotation_minutes.
Sasha: rollout plan: 1) instrumentation + alerts (2 days). 2) controller + shrinkable ephemeral slices (1 week). 3) canary (2 days). 4) review costs + SLO impact -> gradual opt-in (2 weeks).
Mira: also add capability to prefer racks with spare NIC headroom and cooler thermal profile. we can score candidate racks by egress_headroom - thermal_score.
Anand: agree. scheduler scoring function prototype: score = w1*egress_headroom + w2*(1 - hbm_eviction_rate) + w3*thermal_margin. We'll tune weights.
Jonah: please add a prometheus query snippet for alerts. e.g.:
```
sum by(tenant)(rate(egress_bytes[1m])) > 80000000 or sum by(rack)(increase(hbm_evictions[5m])) > 5
```
Tune thresholds later.
Sasha: one more thing: tenants with strict SLA/enterprise contracts should be offered a paid dedicated carveout when pinwheel triggers more than 3 times in a day. link billing event to SRE tickets.
Riley: I'll draft ticket templates and cost calc.
Mira: ok let's do instrumentation first. who's owning the controller PR?
Sasha: I'll take controller + scoring. Anand will do metrics and alerts, Kai will handle scheduler integration, Riley does runbook + billing tie-in. Jonah will observe the canary and own incident comms.
Jonah: thanks. tagging folks: @Sasha @Anand @Kai @Riley. I'll post canary status here after first rotation. :thumbsup:
